spectrum-screen.title: The engineers' spectrum screen
spectrum-screen.caption: A faint 5 on the rural line. The screen draws every bin, so your eye finds the two bumps. The detector reads only the eight keypad bins, and both sit under the 12% bar.

leakage.title: One tone, five bins
leakage.caption: On a bin, the tone fills one bin. Halfway between bins it spreads into every bin. The hatched bars are leakage: matches beyond the two bins nearest the tone.

mid-turn.title: Whole turn, half a turn
mid-turn.caption: The 1,000 Hz dot ends the block back where it started. The 1,500 Hz dot stops half a turn short, so the next sample (the hollow dot) jumps from 1.00 to −1.00.

two-arrows.title: Two arrows make one tone
two-arrows.caption: Each arrow is half size. The mirror arrow is always the counter-clockwise arrow reflected across the horizontal line, so the up-down parts cancel and the left-right parts add to the sample.

leftover.title: The leftover arrow
leftover.caption: Left: the leftover arrow turns 22.5° per sample, half a turn in all, and the chain reaches 64% as far as a full pile. Right: 45° per sample, one whole turn, and the chain closes.

two-chains.title: Two chains per bin
two-chains.caption: The mirror chain can point anywhere on the small circle, depending on where the tone starts. From our start it points 112.5° away and pulls the match down to 60%.

main-lobe.title: The main lobe
main-lobe.caption: This is lesson 10's central hump, now named: the main lobe. It falls to zero one bin out on each side, where the leftover arrow makes one whole turn.

side-lobes.title: The side lobes
side-lobes.caption: Beyond the main lobe the curve rises into side lobes that shrink slowly. The 7's bin and the 1's bin both sit on side lobes of the 770 Hz tone.

keypad-leak.title: A loud 770 Hz across the row bins
keypad-leak.caption: The 7's bin (843.75 Hz) sits on the second side lobe of the 770 Hz curve and catches 13%, over the 12% bar.

phase-wobble.title: Why only sometimes
phase-wobble.caption: The long chain is fixed. The small chains move with the starts, so the end lands somewhere in a small cloud. Filled dots land past the bar: those presses are thrown out.

bar-seesaw.title: No bar fits
bar-seesaw.caption: The two ranges overlap. Hearing the rural keys needs a bar below 7.7%; keeping out the leak needs one above 14.6%.

chain-gap.title: The gap is the top of the fraction
chain-gap.caption: The arrows of a chain all turn by the same angle, so they run around one circle. Measured with that circle's radius as 1, the gap is the top of the fraction and one step is the bottom.

chord.title: The chord
chord.caption: The line from the centre to the chord's midpoint splits the angle x in half and the chord in two halves, each sin(x/2) long.

hann-taper.title: Taper the edges
hann-taper.caption: The window shrinks the arrows near both ends of the block. The plain chain's full-length end arrows leave a wide gap; the Hann chain's short ones leave it nearly closed.

effective-length.title: Half the block does the work
effective-length.caption: A Hann-windowed block acts roughly like one half as long, and its main lobe is twice as wide.

hann-three-curves.title: Three plain chains make the Hann curve
hann-three-curves.caption: Added as arrows, then rescaled so a tone on its bin reads 100%. Each plain curve is zero at every whole bin but its own centre, so the sum is zero everywhere except at −1, 0 and +1 bins.

window-trade.title: The window's trade
window-trade.caption: At 128 samples the Hann main lobe swallows the next row's tone. At 256 samples it stops short of it.

lobe-vs-length.title: Where the bins land
lobe-vs-length.caption: Each mark is one block length. Its height is how close a neighbouring tone lands to the bin you read. For loud keys ten times the faint ones, closer than about 1.75 bins is too close: 224 fails, while 208, 216 and 232 just get through. A hotter line makes taller leaks and needs more room. Every block shorter than 176 fails too.

zero-padding.title: Zero padding
zero-padding.caption: The padded bins fall on exactly the same curve. A bin now sits on the tone, but the leak at 843.75 Hz is unchanged.

padding-myth.title: Padding does not narrow the hump
padding-myth.caption: More dots, same hump. The 770 Hz tone is still inside it at 38%.
